extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and USPTO enrollment & discipline officials (OED staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for imposing reciprocal discipline (exclusion) under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including notice/service, opportunity to respond, bases for discipline, publication, and cross-notification obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the Director may impose reciprocal discipline (e.g., exclusion) identical to discipline imposed by a duly constituted state authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order requested that the Director impose reciprocal discipline upon Respondent identical to the discipline imposed by the New York Supreme Court. Respondent was given an opportunity to respond opposing imposition based on one or more reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for discipline: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6), which proscribes engaging in conduct reflecting adversely on a practitioner's fitness to practice, is a basis for exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states Respondent was excluded for violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) based upon the discipline imposed by the state court. The published Notice of Exclusion identifies the specific regulatory violation as the ground for USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond and consequences of non-response
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent receives a Notice and Order and is provided forty days to file a response opposing reciprocal discipline based on the reasons enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent failed to file a response. In light of the failure to respond, the Director determined there was no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and that exclusion from practice before the Office was appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof and determination standard — 'no genuine issue of material fact'
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not raise a timely response under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Analysis section: 'In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that: (1) there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and (2) exclusion ... is appropriate.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for action
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions imposing discipline are taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly states: 'This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and service requirements (mailing and address)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and Order must be mailed (certified mail indicated) and delivered; certificate of service must show mailing to the respondent's most recent address provided to OED per 37 C.F.R. § 11.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail (receipt no. given) and delivered; the Certificate of Service certifies mailing first class certified mail to the Respondent at the most recent address provided pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public posting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: OED must publish the Final Order and a Notice of Exclusion (including required content) and disciplinary decisions are posted in the OED Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order provisions: (b) the OED DOC shall publish this Final Order; (c) the OED DOC shall publish the following notice in the Official Gazette; and disciplinary decisions are posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room (URL provided). The Notice of Exclusion text demonstrates required content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-notification to other disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED DGC must notify disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the respondent is admitted, courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and the public of the public discipline and reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order (d) directs the OED DGC, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, to give notice of the public discipline and reasons for the discipline to relevant state disciplinary agencies, courts where admitted, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of published Notice of Exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Exclusion must identify the respondent (name, registration number), the regulation violated, the basis for discipline (including the state authority and case citation), and factual basis (e.g., convictions, sentence, forfeiture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published Notice of Exclusion in this matter includes: respondent's name and registration number; that exclusion is ordered for violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6); citation to the New York Appellate Division decision (case name and docket); and factual summary of respondent's guilty plea, crimes charged, sentence, and forfeiture amount. The Notice demonstrates the expected content and level of factual specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal conviction/serious misconduct as basis for state discipline (and thus reciprocal discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent's guilty plea to felony crimes (e.g., conspiracy to commit securities fraud, securities fraud) and resulting sentence and forfeiture can be the factual basis leading to state disbarment and reciprocal USPTO discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice recounts: 'On January 14, 2011 ... Respondent pled guilty to the crimes of insider trading; specifically, conspiracy to commit securities fraud ... and securities fraud ... On June 30, 2011, Respondent was sentenced to thirty months in prison and ordered to forfeit $378,608. The Supreme Court of New York disbarred Mr. Cutillo as a result of his guilty plea ...' This exemplifies conduct that triggers reciprocal discipline.
